Summarise indicators by calendar period

Source: R/summarise_by_interview.R
summarise_by_period.Rd

Summarises the indicators of each unit by month or year, for panels and maps without a survey: hot days per month, the longest spell per year. The statistics follow the registry as in summarise_by_interview(), and a period with less than min_coverage of its days present gives NA.

Usage

summarise_by_period(
  x,
  period = c("month", "year"),
  stats = NULL,
  min_coverage = 0.8,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A long indicator table.

period

"month" or "year".

stats

Optional named list of statistics per kind of indicator, e.g. list(flag = c("sum", "mean"), spell = "max"). Statistics: "sum", "mean", "max", "min", "n" (number of non-missing values).

min_coverage

Share of the window that must be covered by data.

id

<data-masking> Column identifying the survey units; by default the one recorded by prepare_coord().

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

Value

A long c4e_tbl with the unit identifiers, period (the date the period starts) and one column per indicator and statistic, with the new time step.

Examples

x <- update_meta(
  tibble::tibble(ID = "1", date = as.Date("2022-01-01") + 0:59,
                 value = rep(c(28, 31, 33), 20)),
  key = "ID", date_col = "date", shape = "long", unit = "C", time_step = "day")
calc_threshold_day(x, above = 30) |>
  summarise_by_period("month", min_coverage = 0)
#> Using `unit = "C"` from upstream unit.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#> # Context:  value [C], month, long; key ID; 2 indicators
#>   ID    period     day_abv_30_sum C_abv_30_sum
#>   <chr> <date>              <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 1     2022-01-01             20           40
#> 2 1     2022-02-01             19           37
#> 3 1     2022-03-01              1            3
